source.title: An integrated sequential deep learning framework with experience replay for large-scale species distribution modeling under data scarcity
source.authors: Fabián Santos; S. Moreno; Mauricio Mejía-Guerrero; V. Graw

record.file_problem: none; full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out natural-data performance for a sequential DNN in a new domain: multispecies ecological distribution modeling. It does not test the listed memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example versions.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates held-out sensitivity and compares training configurations, but does not report training error alongside test error or test networks on random labels. Results about generalization on natural data are included under fits_no_version; cited findings are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a small batch size partly on the strength of Keskar et al.'s generalization finding, but reports its ecological modeling method's performance without testing any listed version. Natural-data sensitivity alone does not test V1; architecture and dropout comparisons concern sequential-learning stability, without the interpolation analysis required by V2 or a dropout comparison on final held-out error required by V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that integrated sampling and replay-based sequential learning provide stable multispecies predictions across scales and niche breadths, particularly for restricted-tolerance taxa. They emphasize smoother suitability surfaces, extrapolation trade-offs, and the importance of sampling and training design over architecture alone. Stability does not mean equal absolute performance across scales or metrics.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a fully connected sequential DNN with experience replay and evaluates species-distribution predictions; it does not use the original random-label memorization method or test a listed version.
record.method_sensitivity: Sequential-learning stability varied with architecture capacity, learning rate, regularization, and replay-buffer size. Held-out sensitivity differed by evaluation scale, probability threshold, and niche-breadth group.

fits_no_version.finding: Continental median sensitivity was 0.86 for sDNN; national sensitivity was lower, with GLM highest at 0.75. Algorithm rankings also depended on whether sensitivity or the Boyce Index was used.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multispecies ecological prediction performance depends on evaluation scale and metric.

fits_no_version.finding: Buffered sequential training had the highest continental median sensitivity and lowest dispersion, while non-sequential training had higher median Boyce values with frequent negative outliers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequential training and replay can trade sensitivity against suitability-ranking performance in multispecies distribution models.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.3 reports dropout performing comparably to no regularization during sequential learning; larger architectures retained performance better than reduced architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture capacity and regularization choices affect continual-learning stability across species.

record.problems: The study does not report a train-test error gap or random-label memorization test. Some configuration-specific results are presented only in figures; the text gives limited numeric detail for them. Results are for ecological presence-background prediction and are not directly comparable to image or language classification accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No rows qualify for the listed versions: the paper does not report a result measuring their specified behaviors. Figure-only configuration values are not extracted as rows because they do not map to a listed version.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or corresponding held-out chance comparison using the same architecture and training recipe.
No width sweep beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold, convergence check, or corresponding test-error comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
Adam is used without an SGD or momentum-SGD comparison.
Batch size remains 256; no comparison of batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.

Dropout is compared with no regularization for sequential-learning stability, but no isolated dropout effect on final held-out error is reported. Training-set-size and dropout-strength regimes are not tested.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No identification and removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining against matched random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the reader's tests/T3 classification to uses_without_test/T4. No result rows were supplied, and the omitted configuration comparisons are declared in rows_left_out. Figure 8 concerns diagnostic sequential-learning performance; Figure 9 compares training configurations rather than isolating dropout.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or test comparison, and no test of whether the same architecture and recipe fit random labels and generalize on natural labels.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
Only Adam is used; no adaptive-optimizer comparison or held-out comparison under alternative tuning.
Batch size is held at 256; no batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget.
Dropout is compared with a no-regularization control for sequential-learning performance, but the study does not report a dropout effect on held-out error.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other perturbation-based generalization measure.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Uses the small-batch generalization finding to configure its ecological modeling method; its reported results do not directly test V1–V8.

tranche.reason: Section 2.3.2 motivates batch size 256 using Keskar et al.'s generalization finding, but provides no batch-size comparison. Architecture and regularization experiments concern sequential-learning stability and knowledge retention rather than a listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The pack lists no rows, statements, or verdicts. Section 3.3's dropout comparison concerns sequential-learning performance; independent test-set comparisons evaluate training configurations rather than isolate dropout's effect on held-out error.
